The Commission, after careful consideration of the comments of stakeholders and oral submissions/presentation made during the public hearing, has finalised this order attached as **Annexure-I** . Also, the Commission’s analysis of the issues raised by the stakeholders and findings thereon have been discussed in **Annexure-II** attached. Many of the stakeholders whose comments, on certain aspects which are beyond the scope of the draft order, have not been examined in this order. While the stakeholders’ comments and their analysis have been included in the said annexure, the analysis of some of the stakeholders’ comments, on the mode of implementation of this order are examined in the subsequent paragraphs. 11. M/s Essar Renewable Limited (ERL) and Mahindra Susten have submitted that the proposed mechanism creates an entirely new framework overriding the voluntary nature of withdrawal (Regulation 3.7) and relinquishment (Regulation 24.1), imposing mandatory options and deemed surrender on entities with valid LOAs, unrevoked connectivity, and no withdrawal/ relinquishment request. This amounts to a substantive amendment of the GNA Regulations, which could only be effected through the formal process under Section 178 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and not through an order under Regulations 41 and 42. Accordingly, they have proposed that the draft order be withdrawn or at least made optional. 13. M/s Serentica has submitted that the draft order is a positive step and should come into force expeditiously. It has been stated that there have been numerous rounds of public consultations by way of staff paper, written comments on the instant draft order, and a public hearing in the matter, and that the mode of implementation should not halt the entire exercise of releasing the Connectivity. _The Central Commission, for reasons to be recorded in writing, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by an affected party to remove the hardship arising out of the operation of these regulations.”_ _The Central Commission may from time to time issue suo moto orders and practice directions with regards to implementation of these regulations and matters incidental or ancillary thereto, as the case may be.”_ - (4) The entity covered under the final list issued by the CTUIL under para 3 of this Annexure, shall, within 60 days of the issuance of the list, opt for one of the following options for treatment of the Connectivity granted to such entity, failing - (i) Revised final grant of Connectivity to the entity to whom the final grant of Connectivity was issued as on the date of issuance of this order. - (iii) Entities that have already entered into a Connectivity Agreement as of the date of issuance of this order shall sign a supplementary agreement to incorporate the revised intimation. - (i) Twelve months of issuance of revised in-principle intimation or revised final intimation, as the case may be, by the CTUIL under sub-clause (b) of Clause (6)(A) of this Annexure; or - (ii) No Objection Certificate from the concerned REIA that issued LoA1 certifying non-signing of the PPA. - (g) CTUIL shall scrutinize the documents furnished by the entity and, in case the documents are in order, shall issue a revised grant (within two months of the completion of the month in which the application for exercising the option, complete in all respects, has been received by the CTUIL) as under: - (i) Revised final grant of connectivity to the entity to whom the final grant of Connectivity was issued as on the date of issuance of this order. - (ii) Revised in-principle grant of Connectivity to the entity to whom the final grant of Connectivity has not been issued as on the date of issuance of this Order, and only an in-principle grant of Connectivity has been issued as on the date of issuance of this order. - (iii) Entities that have already entered into a Connectivity Agreement as on the date of issuance of this Order shall sign a supplementary agreement to incorporate the revised intimation. - (d) The Conn-BGs shall be kept valid by such entity until CTUIL returns them in terms of this order. The entity may choose to continue to be treated under the extant Regulations by furnishing an intimation to CTUIL within the timeline, as provided under Para 4 of this Annexure. - 4.6.3. Hence, the experience gained in implementing the present order, shall work out as an impact assessment. - 4.9.2. CER, IIT-K has suggested that the draft order does not define the timing, duration, or periodicity of these windows, i.e annual, bi-annual, financial-year based, or would be triggered event-wise upon surrender. - 4.14.1. It is provided that within 60 days of the issuance of this Order, CTUIL shall issue a detailed modality of auction after stakeholders’ consultation and submit the same information to the Commission. In case of any discrepancies in the detailed procedure of CTUIL, the Commission shall issue the necessary directions as required in terms of Regulation 39.1 of the GNA Regulations. ### **List of stakeholders who submitted their comments on the draft Order in Petition No. 11/SM/2026**
